page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-8GB is a compute-focused virtual machine instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, along with 100 GB of bundled local SSD storage. A single public IPv4 address is included by default, and no discrete graphics hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-threaded compute and compression throughput. The AMD EPYC 9575F processor delivers top 10% results in single-core stress-ng tests (3870.68) and single-threaded gzip compression (37.98 GB/sec), as well as strong Geekbench single-core performance (2220.0). Text processing capabilities also register in the top decile. In contrast, multi-threaded CPU results, PassMark CPU scores, and software compilation throughput remain in the average tier across comparable instances, while PassMark memory performance is in the lower quartile.

Because the server utilizes shared CPU resource allocation with a 1:2 RAM ratio, it yields high compute density and per-thread speed without the overhead of dedicated hypervisor reservations. The primary architectural tradeoff is limited memory headroom and lower uncached memory benchmark throughput relative to memory-intensive configurations.

UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-8GB fits compute-bound single-threaded tasks, continuous integration and build nodes, microservice APIs, static web serving, and small-footprint batch data compression pipelines that do not require dedicated vCPU reservations or large in-memory footprints.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-8GB is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization. Configured with 4 shared vCPUs, 8.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), and 100 GB of local SSD storage, this instance targets workloads with a 1:2 memory-to-core profile. It features exceptional single-threaded compute, showing top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng and compression benchmarks, alongside strong Geekbench single-core scores. Multi-threaded processing and static web serving throughput align with mid-tier industry averages, while memory benchmarks indicate constrained throughput under heavy memory-bus saturation. Lacking a discrete GPU, the instance offers a resource-efficient footprint for compilation, web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and single-threaded compute workloads.
